title: Going to the Airport
subtitle: Emma's sister is flying in at six, and the traffic is bad.
description: An A1 reading and listening text about an airport trip: time, directions and the words you need at arrivals.
source: authored for this site; no source document
passage: My sister Kate is coming from Ohio today. Her plane arrives at six o'clock in the evening.
The airport is far — forty minutes by car, more when the traffic is bad. Jack drives. We leave at half past four, because I do not want to be late.
The traffic is bad. Of course it is. We arrive at ten past five and we park the car.
Inside, I look at the big screen. Flight 412 from Columbus: on time. We have fifty minutes, so we buy two coffees and we wait.
At six o'clock the people start coming out. I see Kate with a small bag and a very tired face.
“Long,” she says. “And the man next to me talked for two hours.”
We walk to the car. Outside it is cold and dark, and it is good to have her here.

exercises.title: Travel Words
exercises.instructions: Complete each sentence with one word.

items.prompt: The ___ was bad, so we were slow.
items.explanation: Traffic is all the cars on the road.
To arrive is to get to a place.

items.prompt: The flight is not late. It is ___ ___.
items.explanation: On time means not early and not late.

items.prompt: The airport is ___ from our apartment — forty minutes by car.
items.explanation: Far means a long way away.

items.prompt: We ___ for fifty minutes and drank coffee.
items.explanation: To wait is to stay until something happens.
